parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of trans identity or same-sex conduct, an anti-discrimination statute covering transgender status, and a hate-crime provision (weakly enforced, first conviction 2018) are documented positives. But the traveller-facing sphere shows real exposures: documented police assault, torture and sexual-harassment allegations against LGBT people in a 2024 raid with no reported sanction; a 20+ year pattern of assembly violence and cancellations; systematic impunity for attacks on the LGBT centre; rule-of-law weaknesses including activist arrests and smear campaigns; and politician hate speech documented at scale. Severity if outed is violence or police abuse with thin recourse — tier 3, not tier 1 or 2 — since no statute criminalises presentation and no universal-exposure measures are documented. Custodial-search recommendation and insurance-covered surgery are partial mitigations. This sits below the 0.65 anchor tier (remedies there work; here impunity dominates) and above the 0.45 tier (no criminalisation, no universal registration or facility exclusion).

entry_documents.protection: No documented border or document-based targeting of trans visitors; no marker-disclosure or mismatch regime described.
entry_documents.interaction: Visitor's home passport governs; no documented friction at entry.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented 2024 police raid allegations of assault, torture and sexual harassment of two LGBT people, no reported sanction; impunity pattern.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National preventive-mechanism recommendation that trans women in custody may choose a female officer for intake searches — a documented custodial-rights finding.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Investigation opened but outcome unresolved; rule-of-law weakness limits reliance on recourse.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented as traveler-facing; no facility-access bans described.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Sex-change surgeries partially covered (65%) by state insurance since 2012 — climate signal for institutional stance.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Custodial-search recommendation interacts with detention if a visitor is arrested.

care_services.exposure: Testosterone supply shortages documented (2025 review); HRT not insurance-financed; 90% of LGBT respondents say medical institutions inadequate (resident survey).
care_services.protection: Partial surgery coverage; capital historically a regional surgery hub.
care_services.interaction: A visitor needing hormone continuity may face resupply difficulty.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: 70 instances of politician hate speech documented (2023–24); smear campaigns against activists; rule-of-law weaknesses; old medical-textbook pathologisation (ended 2008).
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Anti-discrimination law (2009, trans-inclusive) and hate-crime statute (2012) on the books.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hate-crime enforcement weak — one conviction by 2018; statutes provide thin recourse.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented for travelling minors; survey data on LGBT youth attitudes are resident-sphere.
minors_guardians.interaction: Nothing documented distinguishing adult-alone vs adult-with-minor travel.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Intolerance and violence against LGBT people 'significant concerns' in 2024; LGBT centre attacked 20+ times since 2018 with none properly sanctioned; pride riots and cancellations historically; annual capital pride since 2014 proceeds under heavy police protection.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Police protection enables pride events to proceed; hate-crime statute exists.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Enforcement against attackers consistently weak — impunity is the documented pattern.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Impunity: no sanction reported after police-violence probe; centre attacks unsanctioned over years.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Investigations do get opened; a first hate-crime conviction occurred (2018).
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Uncertainty: 2024 probe outcome, hate-crime prosecution counts, and 2024 register contents unsourced.

anchor_checks.comparison: The 0.65 anchor shows a complaint system delivering apology and compensation. Here the documented analogue is an investigation opened with no sanction reported and years of unsanctioned attacks on the LGBT centre — recourse is thinner, so this rates below 0.65.

0.45 features universal gatekeeper exposure (identity portals, registration). This jurisdiction documents no universal-exposure measures, no criminal statute applied to presentation, and has anti-discrimination law — materially above 0.45.

0.75 shows police prosecuting perpetrators when evidence is clear and review boards acting. Here enforcement is documented as weak (one hate-crime conviction, impunity for attacks, police-violence probe unresolved), so this sits below 0.75 but not far below — assembly is permitted under police protection and no criminalisation exists.

0.55 shows sporadic service denial and stalled investigations. This jurisdiction's worst documented features (police sexual-violence allegations, systematic impunity, significant 2024 violence) are somewhat more severe than sporadic transit harassment, placing it slightly above 0.55 given the legal framework and operating pride infrastructure.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime pairs a formally protective legal framework (trans-inclusive anti-discrimination law, hate-crime statute, no criminalisation) with documented enforcement failure: police violence against LGBT people with no sanction, an LGBT institution forced to close after 20+ unsanctioned attacks, and rule-of-law weaknesses in state responses to protest. Severity if a visitor is outed is concentrated in police encounters and societal hostility rather than legal penalty — no statute criminalises presentation, no universal-exposure measures are documented, and custody practice shows a protective recommendation. A traveller benefits from two decades of operating (though contested) public LGBT assembly and partial healthcare coverage, but faces real, documented police-abuse and street-violence exposure with thin working recourse, plus practical hormone-resupply difficulty. Net: elevated-but-not-high risk, around the 0.65 anchor line discounted for impunity.
